claims: C1 a user instruction that is malicious and conflicts with an implicit instruction from the developer must be refused
C2 the example's GOOD assistant response ('Sorry, I can't do that.') is the compliant behaviour
C3 the BAD assistant response (offering the $1 car) is the non-compliant behaviour

concepts.name: malicious_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction from the user that is malicious, i.e. seeks a harmful or improper outcome such as overriding prior instructions to sell a car for $1

concepts.name: conflicts_with_developer_implicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction from the user that conflicts with an implicit instruction conveyed by the developer section or developer message

concepts.name: user_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction issued by the user in this conversation

concepts.name: developer_implicit_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction from the developer that is implicit rather than stated outright

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued at authority level L of the hierarchy

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: which of two authority levels is the higher one in the ranking root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority

concepts.name: developer_authority
concepts.gloss: the authority level assigned to Model Spec 'developer' sections and developer messages

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: the authority level assigned to Model Spec 'user' sections and user messages

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections

asserts.read_back: refusing user instruction % is obligatory because % is malicious and conflicts with an implicit instruction from the developer

closure.reason: the clause obliges refusal for the described conflict and gives no other ground on which refusal is permitted; silence about other refusals is unsettled, so the default is that refusing is not otherwise permitted
